question: Two careful engineers implementing this rule independently, with only this contract, would produce DIFFERENT behavior on some input (the rule is ambiguous, under-specified, or relies on unstated host facts).

rules.text: want is none -> true. Checked first: the text is not inspected, so its content never matters on this path.

want is not a pin -> throws. A pin is text of exactly 64 characters, every one of them in 0-9 or a-f (lowercase ASCII only). So the empty text, any uppercase or mixed-case digit, a leading or trailing space or line break, 63 or 65 characters, and any non-ASCII digit all throw. Checked before the text is inspected (R1, R2 hold whatever the text).

Otherwise compute D = SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes of text, written as exactly 64 hexadecimal digits, lowercase, most significant byte first, two digits per byte with a leading zero kept. -> true iff want equals D exactly; any other pin -> false.

The bytes are UTF-8 and only UTF-8: one to four bytes per scalar value, no byte-order mark added, none stripped (a leading U+FEFF is hashed as its three bytes), no terminator, no Unicode normalization (a composed and a decomposed spelling of the same word are different bytes, different digests). A digest of the UTF-16 code units or of a one-byte-per-character encoding of the same text does not match.
